points.description: States what extension headers are: optional additional network-layer information/headers that extend the fixed (main) IPv6 header.
points.partial_credit: Vague but on track (e.g. just 'extra headers') earns about half.

points.description: States location: between the fixed/main IPv6 header and the payload/upper-layer (transport) header.
points.partial_credit: Says only 'after the main header' or 'before the payload' earns about half.

points.description: Gives one valid main advantage: new options can be added without changing the base header, OR packets with options are processed faster/simpler by intermediate routers since most extension headers are ignored (except Hop-by-Hop), unlike IPv4 where options are processed by all routers.
points.partial_credit: Vague advantage such as 'more flexible' or 'more efficient' earns about half.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all three parts: what they are, where they sit, and one valid advantage, in any wording. Give part marks for vague but relevant statements. Wrong extra remarks cost nothing unless they contradict a central idea. Round the total to the nearest quarter.
